description: This file defines the Perl module 'Mail::Address', which provides functionalities for parsing, constructing, and manipulating email address strings and related components such as names and comments. It includes methods for extracting names, formatting addresses, and accessing address parts like host and user.

classes.name: Mail::Address
classes.description: A class representing an email address with methods for parsing, formatting, and extracting components such as name, host, and user.

methods.name: _extract_name
methods.description: Attempts to extract a person's name from a comment or phrase, cleaning and adjusting casing accordingly.

methods.name: _tokenise
methods.description: Splits an address string into tokens for parsing.

methods.name: _find_next
methods.description: Finds the next relevant token in the token list during parsing.

methods.name: _complete
methods.description: Constructs a new address object from parsed phrase, address, and comment components.

methods.name: new
methods.description: Constructs a new Mail::Address object with provided components.

methods.name: parse
methods.description: Parses a raw address string into a Mail::Address object, extracting phrase, address, and comments.

methods.name: phrase
methods.description: Getter/setter for the phrase part of the address.

methods.name: address
methods.description: Getter/setter for the email address part.

methods.name: comment
methods.description: Getter/setter for comment parts associated with the address.

methods.name: set_or_get
methods.description: Internal method to set or get components of the object.

methods.name: format
methods.description: Formats one or multiple addresses into a string suitable for email headers.

methods.name: name
methods.description: Attempts to extract the display name from the address or comments.

methods.name: host
methods.description: Extracts the host (domain) part from the email address.

methods.name: user
methods.description: Extracts the user (local part) from the email address.
